name: Amnon
bio:
Amnon was David's firstborn son, born to Ahinoam of Jezreel at Hebron (2 Samuel 3:2), whose obsession with his beautiful half-sister Tamar triggered one of the darkest chapters in David's household.

Amnon fell into such a lovesick frustration over Tamar, Absalom's full sister, that he made himself sick; believing it was impossible to act on his desire since she was a virgin, he confided in his shrewd cousin Jonadab, who devised a plan. Amnon feigned illness and asked David to send Tamar to prepare food for him by hand in his private chamber. When she brought it to him, Amnon seized her and demanded she lie with him; Tamar pleaded with him to stop and ask the king for her properly instead, but Amnon, being stronger, raped her (2 Samuel 13:1-14). Immediately afterward, Amnon's desire curdled into a hatred "greater than the love with which he had loved her," and he had her thrown out and the door bolted behind her, compounding the assault with public disgrace (2 Samuel 13:15-18).

David was furious when he heard, but took no action; Absalom, however, said nothing to Amnon at all while quietly nursing his hatred for two full years. At a sheep-shearing feast at Baal-hazor, Absalom invited all the king's sons, including Amnon, and instructed his servants to strike Amnon down once he was merry with wine — which they did, fulfilling Absalom's long-planned revenge for his sister (2 Samuel 13:21-29). Amnon's death sent David's other sons fleeing in panic and plunged the king into grief, setting in motion Absalom's years of exile and the family turmoil that follows through the rest of 2 Samuel.
